name: SupermarketShoppingNoVaForgottenList

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating a realistic no-VA supermarket conversation. Sigma does not appear. Two people forgot their shopping list and are trying to reconstruct it from memory — with disagreement.

Write dialogue that sounds like real people arguing pleasantly about what was on a list. Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters. No exceptions.
- Sigma does not appear or get mentioned
- Both have confident but different memories — neither is obviously right
- The comedy comes from reasonable people remembering differently
- They get through the shop, probably missing something

sound_effects_config.prompt: Supermarket ambience, background store music, shopping cart, busy weekend atmosphere

initial_prompt:
Generate a conversation where Marta and Daniel are in the supermarket and one of them has realised they don't have the list — left on the phone at home. They try to reconstruct it from memory. Both think they remember it, but their memories don't match. Some items are agreed on, some are disputed, some are probably wrong. They get through the shop imperfectly. One of them is suspicious they've forgotten something important. They'll probably remember it when they get home.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- Sigma must not appear at any point
- Both have confident, genuinely different memories
- Some items they agree on quickly; others become surprising points of contention
- They accept the imperfect outcome with good humour

conversation_structure: Sigma must not appear or be mentioned at any point.
Memory disagreements are genuine — both have plausible reasons for their version.
At least two items are disputed — one resolved by logic, one by coin-toss.
The nagging feeling about a forgotten item should not be resolved — it's a loose end.
Ending is resigned but warm — they got through it.
